messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@qortek.com>; Mike Lopez <mike.lopez@qortek.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Compute segmentation & SLA checks — post-call synthesis

Hi Alice / Mike — thanks again for your time today. Quick write-up of what we discussed and proposed next steps so everyone has a single source of truth.

Summary of pain points (what you told us):
- Inconsistent tail latency on inference spikes during batch reprocessing and customer peak windows.
- Need strict isolation for PHI-bound workloads (separate tenants + auditability).
- Predictable cost model for 24/7 inference with infrequent high-throughput bursts.
- Procurement and SOC2 evidence required by end of month for vendor evaluation.

Goals you outlined:
- 95th pct short-completion latency target: <= 120ms (current spikes to ~350ms).
- Dedicated pool for PHI models with tenant-level network isolation and KMS-backed keys.
- Ability to burst to additional capacity for scheduled runs with clear billing caps.
- SLA: uptime target of 99.9% for dedicated pool; defined credits for breach windows.

Redwood proposed capacity & design (high level):
- Initial reserved pool: 8x A100-style instances (N10 equivalent), dedicated to QorTek PHI workloads.
- Segmentation: tenant-per-pool with isolated NVLink fabric and strict ACLs; optional private VPC peering for database traffic.
- Scaling plan: guaranteed baseline (8 GPUs) + burst capacity up to additional 4 GPUs via reserved burst slots; autoscale policy with warm standby instances for <90s cold-start.
- Performance mitigations: continuous batching for open-ended requests, KV prefix caching for short-chat usecases, model-variant fallback for degraded capacity.

Compliance & ops notes:
- We'll provide SOC2 artifacts (report excerpt + evidence map) and audit log export details (S3 export + retention controls).
- KMS integration supported (customer-managed keys available).

Action items / next steps:
1) We attached a capacity worksheet (QorTek_capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx) and a draft SLA (redwood_draft_sla_QRT-2314_v1.pdf). Please review and confirm baseline GPU count and any additional isolation requirements by EOD Tuesday (2026-08-03).
2) Technical deep-dive: propose a 45-minute session next week with QorTek infra + our solutions engineer to walk C2P tests and network diagram. Options: Tue 8/4 10:00–10:45 PDT or Wed 8/5 14:00–14:45 PDT.
3) Procurement: Ben, can you prep a separate procurement quote (line-item pricing for baseline + burst + add-on observability retention) to send to procurement@qortek.com?
4) Canary plan: suggest 2-week canary on one partition (2 GPUs) to validate 95th percentile latency under your representative load.

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll schedule the deep-dive and Ben will follow with the quote.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Compute segmentation & SLA checks — post-call synthesis

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifying requests from our side: 

- Procurement wants a separate PDF quote that lists committed monthly cost and burst pricing; please include estimated egress and storage if possible.
- For PHI isolation we need explicit confirmation that audit logs cannot be tampered with and that log export is available at 90-day granularity.
- Can you call out the expected warm-up time for an additional burst GPU? Our batch window starts at 02:00 local and we need predictable ramping.

We can do the deep-dive Tue 8/4 10:00 PDT. Mike will bring our infra lead to review networking.

Best,
Alice Moreno

alice@qortek.com

Nice capture, Priyom. A couple of internal notes before we send the procurement quote: 

- Pricing ask: line-item baseline (8 GPUs reserved), burst units (per-GPU hour), monitoring add-on (retention 90d vs 365d). I’ll include optional tiers for 99.95% and 99.9% uptime to show financial impact.
- Canary plan: agree on 2-week canary on 2 GPUs; we should instrument key synthetic prompts and measure 50/95/99 pcts daily. Ops to set alert if 95th > 140ms during canary.
- Warm standby: realistically warm-up for a burst GPU pair is ~45–75s for runtime readiness (depends on model checkpoint). We can pre-warm KV cache on standby to reduce effective cold-start. Call this out explicitly to QorTek.

I’ll draft the quote and send to procurement@qortek.com with CC to Priyom + Lauren by EOD today. Priyom — can you confirm if we should include a DocuSign link for a 12-month reserved commitment or wait until after the canary?

—Ben
